To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the redox‐midpotentials of flavin‐contaning photoreceptors can be altered by site‐directed mutation, and that this is an important factor in determining the primary photochemistry of these proteins.
the midpoint potential of FAD in the BLUF‐domain of AppA is ∼260 mV and that this potential can be shifted to more positive values through structure‐directed mutational changes.

the midpoint potential of a flavin chromophore in solution is −0.25 V, and that the redox‐midpotentials of flavin in the BLUF, LOV and Cryptochrome domains are, respectively, −0.26, −0.29, and −0.33 V.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the structure and function of flavin‐based blue light photoreceptors.

the elucidation of the structure of the BLUF‐domain photoreceptor protein from Rhodobater sphaeroidens (RsbUVR2), which is a member of the blue light sensor (BLUF) family of flavin‐based photoreceptors.
the elucidation of structure‐function relationships in the BLUF‐domain‐containing photoproteins, which have been found in a variety of bacteria, fungi and cyanobacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BLUF domains have the highest sensitivity for chemical reduction in the absence of light and the LOV domains have the lowest sensitivity.
the BLUF domain has the highest redox midpoint potential among all flavin‐containg photosensory receptors and LOV domains have the lowest redox midpoint potential.
the midpoint potential of BLUF domains is intermediate between LOV domains and cryptochromes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the BLUF domain is a flavin‐controlling photoreceptor that is sensitive to intracellular reduction, while LOV domains are not.
the redox‐midpotentials of BLUF domains and Cryptochrome domains are more sensitive to changes in the chemical environment of their flavin chromophores than LOV domains.
the redox‐midpoints of the FADs in the three flavin‐photoreceptor families are in a sequence: BLUF domains < LOV domains < Cryptochromes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the midpoint potential of FAD in a photoreceptor protein is not a fixed value but can vary significantly.

the redox‐midpotentials of flavin‐containg photoreceptors are not as disparate as previously thought, and that the redox potentials of the FAD cofactor are not a good predictor of photochemical mechanism.
BLUF domains, like LOV domains, are capable of undergoing photochemistry in the presence of chemical reducing agents.
